rates.source: The rates of the crews of a site (plan 0006, D1): the work of one crew in one day (the unit of each work is its unit), for each method of a site (D6). The norms of Việt Nam (Định mức dự toán xây dựng công trình, Phụ lục II of Thông tư 12/2021/TT-BXD) give the days of people for each unit of work, but the chapters of the concrete, the masonry and the finish were not found (2026-11-10): each rate is an estimate with its reason. The method 1974 has no machine: the people mix the concrete on the site and carry the materials up the path of the hill (priv/history/tuong_chua_kito_vua_cong_truong.json, the facts carry and scaffold_hard).

design.source: estimate: a sculptor and a helper make the model of the figure, in 30 days in a computer with a print (today), in 90 days in clay at a small scale (1974)

survey.source: estimate: two surveyors set out a site of a statue in 2 days with a total station (today), in 5 days with a tape and a level (1974)

concrete.source: estimate: a pump and a crew of six place about 25 m3 of a small pour in a day; with no machine, a crew of twelve mixes the concrete by hand and carries it up the scaffold in buckets, about 4 m3 in a day

formwork.source: estimate: four carpenters set about 40 m2 of curved plywood forms in a day (today), 20 m2 of timber boards cut by hand (1974)

strip.source: estimate: the forms come off in about a third of the time to set them

scaffold.source: estimate: the face of a scaffold of steel frames, about 60 m2 in a day for three people; of wooden poles and bamboo, hard to set up on the rock of the hill (the fact scaffold_hard), about 25 m2

rebar.source: estimate: two steel fixers cut, bend and tie about 600 kg of bars in a day with a bender (today), 400 kg by hand (1974)

render.source: estimate: a render of washed stone (đá rửa) on a curved face, about 20 m2 in a day for four people (today), 12 m2 (1974)

carve.source: estimate: the face, the hair and the hands, cut in the concrete and the render by three sculptors

relief.source: estimate: a relief with figures on a panel of the base, by three sculptors

steel.source: estimate: two smiths make and set about 150 kg of the steel of a halo or a grille in a day (today), 60 kg (1974)

stair.source: estimate: three masons cast and set about 10 steps of a spiral stair in a day (today), 4 (1974)

rail.source: estimate: two masons set about 4 m of a rail with its balusters in a day (today), 2 m (1974)

brick.source: estimate: a mason and a helper lay about 1,000 bricks in a day

paint.source: estimate: a painter gives one coat to about 60 m2 of a wall in a day with a roller (today), 40 m2 with a brush (1974)

roof.source: estimate: two roofers fix about 60 m2 of steel sheets in a day

crane.source: estimate: four riggers and a mobile crane set up (or take down) a small tower crane of about 45 m in 3 days; the sites of 1974 had no tower crane

remove.source: estimate: to take down a part takes a third of the days to make it with the machines of today (a breaker, a crane), a half by hand (1974); the amount is the days of the task that made it

task.source: estimate: a task with no work in data takes one hour of a day of 8 hours (the parts of a vehicle at a factory)

cures.source: The waits of a site after a task (plan 0006, D2): the concrete sets before the next task on it. ACI 347R-14 lets the forms of a wall come off after 12 hours over 10 °C; the other days are estimates for the heat of Vũng Tàu.

lift.source: estimate: the next band of a cast waits until the band under it holds it and its forms

strip.source: ACI 347R-14 (12 hours for a wall); the forms of timber of 1974 stay longer (estimate)

set.source: estimate: the figure starts on the base after its concrete has the most of its strength for the load of the scaffold

takeoff.source: The work of a task from its takeoff (World.Drawing.materials/3, the units of priv/places.json): a unit of a material is this much of a work.
